title: Moggallana's powers
hook: foremost in psychic power, and still humble

segments.voice: Yesterday: Sariputta, the general of the dhamma, and your line, wisdom explains. Today, the other friend of the pact, Kolita, now called Moggallana.

On the path down from Vulture Peak, the hill outside Rajagaha, Moggallana smiles. His companion on the walk, Lakkhana, notices and asks what any friend would ask: why the smile? And Moggallana, who in the texts could see things no one around him saw, doesn't answer. Not here, he says. Ask me again when we're with the Buddha. That small refusal on a dusty path is a good door into a man whose powers were famous. The texts care about what he could do. They seem to care even more about how he carried it.
screen: `A SMILE ON THE PATH.` → `WHY THE SMILE?` → `NOT HERE. ASK ME LATER.`

segments.voice: First, the reputation. In the Anguttara Nikaya's list of foremost disciples, the Buddha names Moggallana foremost in psychic power. Earlier on this path we watched him, in another discourse, shake a palace of the gods with his toe. Second, the smile explained. Later, before the Buddha, Lakkhana asks again, and now Moggallana tells it: on the path he saw a suffering being, a body of bones, tormented by birds as it moved through the air. And the Buddha backs him up. In paraphrase: I saw that being too, once, but I didn't speak of it. Others wouldn't have believed me, and that would have been to their harm. So the power is real in the story, and so is the restraint. Say it when it can help, and not before. Third, his slips. In a whole chapter of the Samyutta Nikaya, Moggallana tells his fellow monks how his own meditation went. He reached a deep stillness, and lost it. Distraction crept back in. And the Buddha, he says, came to him and said: Moggallana, don't be careless. Then the next stage, and the same thing again. He ends, in paraphrase: if anyone is a disciple who reached greatness with the teacher's help, it's me. The strongest one in the room, telling everyone where he kept falling. Fourth, the mirror. In the Majjhima Nikaya he teaches monks to check themselves the way someone looks in a mirror: seeing a smudge on their face, they wipe it off, and seeing none, they're glad. Power, in his hands, keeps turning back into honesty about himself.
screen: `FOREMOST IN PSYCHIC POWER.` · `A SMILE, AND A WAIT.` · `HE TELLS WHERE HE SLIPPED.` · `A MIRROR FOR YOUR OWN FACE.` · then, large: `POWER, HUMBLY.`

segments.voice: Name one thing you're good at, cooking, spreadsheets, calming a crying child, and let yourself admit it's real. Then, like Moggallana, recall one time that strength slipped, or someone helped you get it back, and hold both at once, the strength and the help, as you rest with the breath.
Moggallana's powers. Named foremost in psychic power, he holds back what he sees until it can help, tells where he slipped, and teaches the mirror. Today's word.
Your line: power, humbly. The strongest one told everyone where he slipped. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: In Theravada communities Moggallana is honored with Sariputta as one of the Buddha's two chief disciples, and in some temples their images stand on either side of the Buddha.

what a scholar hears: in a chapter of the Samyutta Nikaya given to him, he describes slipping at stage after stage of meditation, and the Buddha warning him each time not to be careless.

chat.says: If Moggallana had amazing powers, why didn't he tell Lakkhana what he saw?
options: He waited until they were with the Buddha, saying it only when it could help.
He was ashamed of his powers and never spoke about them to anyone.
He couldn't remember what he saw once the vision had passed.
chat.meaning: Before the Buddha he told it, and the Buddha said he'd seen that being too but kept quiet. Speak when it can help, not before.

Lakkhana.meaning: a monk who walked with Moggallana and asked about his smile

Moggallana.meaning: one of the two chief disciples, foremost in psychic power

Majjhima Nikaya.meaning: the Middle-Length Sayings, a collection of discourses

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 1.189 (Etadagga Vagga: foremost in psychic power)

notes: All material paraphrased. Confirm SN 19.1: Moggallana smiles descending Vulture Peak; tells Lakkhana to ask in the Buddha's presence; the Buddha says he too had seen that being but did not speak, since others would not believe and it would be to their harm.

Confirm SN 40.1–9: Moggallana's account of losing each jhana and the formless attainments, the Buddha coming by psychic power with 'do not be negligent', and his closing claim to be a disciple who reached greatness of direct knowledge with the Teacher's help.
MN 15 (Anumana Sutta) is spoken by Moggallana; confirm the mirror simile wording as paraphrased.
Confirm the AN 1 sutta number (numbering varies by edition). 'Shake a palace with his toe' refers back to MN 37 (year two, day 432).
howItsDone: confirm the description of the two chief disciples' images flanking the Buddha; it is phrased as 'often'.
